key_insight: Hierarchical multipoint anchoring strengthens buried interfaces in inverted perovskite solar cells, improving efficiency and resistance to thermal cycling.
engineering_relevance: Engineering adhesion at self-assembled monolayer interfaces offers a route to reduce thermo-mechanical failure in high-efficiency perovskite photovoltaics.
method: Pretreat transparent conductive oxides with a homometallic halide to guide ordered self-assembled monolayer formation.
Increase surface hydroxyl density to strengthen metal–oxygen coordination.
Add cooperative chloride-induced hydrogen bonding for robust multipoint anchoring.
evidence_signal: Devices achieved 27.3% efficiency (26.9% certified) and retained 94% of initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between −40 and 85 °C under ISOS-T-3.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish large-area manufacturing compatibility or durability under combined outdoor stresses.
paper_title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
